chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid al-Aqta who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: No one has enlivened our remembrance and the narrations of my father (peace be upon him) except Zurara, Abu Basir Layth al-Muradi, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli. And if it were not for these four, no one would be able to derive (jurisprudential rulings) from this. These are the protectors of the religion and the trustees of my father (peace be upon him) regarding the Halal of Allah and His Haram. And they are the foremost to us in this world and the foremost to us in the hereafter.

key_terms.أَحَادِيثَ أَبِي: narrations of my father (referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir)
key_terms.حَلَالِ اللَّهِ وَ حَرَامِهِ: the Halal of Allah and His Haram (divine law)

ai.seo_question: Who are the four main trustees of the Prophet's family mentioned in Rijal al-Kashshi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi highlights the 'Four Companions' (Al-Asnā) as the foundational pillars of Shia hadith transmission, emphasizing their unique role in preserving the Imam's teachings. Al-Sadiq (AS) elevates them from mere narrators to 'trustees of divine law,' establishing their authority in deriving jurisprudence and ensuring the continuity of religious knowledge. Their designation as 'predecessors' underscores their spiritual and scholarly precedence in both this world and the hereafter.
